Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

OPENS Ch 21: BOOK-CLOSING DOXOLOGY — the chapter's opening transition from systematic-doctrine to liturgical-praise. The doxological-genre-shift parallels the standard-biblical-book-ending pattern: ROMANS 16:25-27 (Pauline final-doxology); JUDE 24-25 (Jude's closing benediction); REVELATION 22:20-21 (John's concluding maranatha-and-grace-formula); 1 ENOCH 108 (the Mäṣḥafä Hēnok γ.4.4 final-chapter-doxology); JUBILEES 50:13 (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle γ.4.5 final-Sabbath-doxology). Meqabyan 2 Mq's closing-doxology STRUCTURALLY PARALLELS 1 Mq 36's closing-tricolon (the dead rise + righteous reign + wicked judged at 1 Mq 36:45 doctrinal-capstone): both books end with eschatology-praise. The Tewahedo liturgical tradition incorporates 2 Mq 21 into Sǝnkǝsar (Synaxarium) commemorative-readings of the Maccabean-martyrs' feast-days. The chapter's praise-orientation redirects the systematic-doctrinal-treatise (Chs 14-20) toward doxological-formation rather than catechetical-instruction.

The Meqabyan double-amen locates the trilogy within the canonical-Hebrew-Bible-and-LXX-Psalter-doxological-tradition + the Tewahedo-EOTC liturgical book-closing convention.
